aiAnalyses.testName: › chromium › ui/dedup-demo.spec.js › Dedup Demo › broken selector always fails — dedup demo @regression
aiAnalyses.summary: The test 'broken selector always fails — dedup demo' intentionally uses a non-existent CSS selector '#this-element-does-not-exist' and asserts it is visible. The element is never present in the DOM, causing the locator to time out after 3000ms and the assertion to fail. This appears to be a deliberately broken test case, likely used to demonstrate deduplication behavior in the reporting framework.
aiAnalyses.likelyRootCause: The locator '#this-element-does-not-exist' is intentionally invalid — no element with this ID exists in the application under test. The test is designed to always fail as a demonstration or regression fixture for the playwright-spec-doc-reporter dedup demo suite. This is not a flaky or environment-related failure; it is a permanently failing test by design.
aiAnalyses.suggestedRemediation: If this test is intentionally broken for demo/dedup purposes, mark it with `test.fail()` so Playwright expects the failure and the suite remains green. If it was meant to test a real element, replace the selector with a valid, stable locator that targets an element actually rendered by the application. Do not use placeholder or stub selectors in production test suites.

structuredFeedback.reasoning: The selector '#this-element-does-not-exist' is a stub/placeholder that will never match any DOM element. The test name itself ('broken selector always fails') confirms this is intentional. The correct remediation depends on intent: (1) if this is a demo of a failing test, wrap with test.fail() to signal expected failure; (2) if this was meant to target a real element, the locator must be corrected to match an actual element in the rendered page.
